newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's scandal-hit justice minister suspended.
newsitem.headline: Russia's scandal-hit justice minister suspended.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin formally suspended Russian Justice Minister Valentin Kovalyov on Wednesday pending an investigation into media allegations that the minister was filmed in a gangland sauna with naked women.
Yeltsin's decree, published by the Kremlin press service, said the suspension took immediate effect. It gave no indication of how long it might last.
The decree said Kovalyov was suspended temporarily "in connection with the need to carry out an investigation into media publications which discredit the minister".

The monthly newspaper Sovershenno Sekretno (Top Secret) last week published grainy snaps taken from a video which it said showed Kovalyov with naked women in September 1995 in the sauna of a gangland nightclub.
Kovalyov, a former Communist, became justice minister in January 1995. He has denied doing anything wrong but had asked the president to suspend him from duties while he cleared his name.
Itar-Tass news agency said on Tuesday the Russian government had asked Yeltsin to sack Kovalyov over the allegations rather than just suspend him.

The scandal was the first sex-linked row involving a senior government official in post-Soviet Russia. Kovalyov, 53, is a member of the Kremlin's top-level Security Council which advises Yeltsin on key policy matters.

Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov, indicating he believed the tape was genuine, said it had been seized by police earlier this year when they arrested a Moscow banker for theft. He said its disclosure was an attempt to undermine the case.
